A [[cuisine]] is a specific set of [[cooking]] traditions and practices, often associated with a specific [[culture]] or region. Each cuisine involves [[Outline of food preparation|food preparation]] in a particular style, of [[food]] and [[drink]] of particular types, to produce individually consumed items or distinct meals. A cuisine is frequently named after the region or place where it originated.  A cuisine is primarily influenced by the ingredients that are available locally or through trade. [[Food and drink prohibitions#Causes|Religious food laws]] can also exercise a strong influence on such culinary practices.

== Regional and ethnic cuisines ==
[[Global cuisine]] is a cuisine that is practiced around the world. A cuisine is a characteristic style of cooking practices and traditions,<ref>[http://www.thefreedictionary.com/cuisine Cuisine (definition)]. Thefreedictionary.com. Accessed June 2011.</ref> often associated with a specific region, country<ref>{{cite web | url=http://oxforddictionaries.com/us/definition/american_english/cuisine?q=cuisine | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131215195627/http://www.oxforddictionaries.com/us/definition/american_english/cuisine?q=cuisine | url-status=dead | archive-date=15 December 2013 | title=Cuisine (definition) | publisher=Oxford Dictionaries | access-date=2013-05-26}}</ref> or culture. To become a global cuisine, a local, regional or national cuisine must spread around the world with its food served worldwide.

[[Regional cuisine]] is based upon national, state or local regions.<ref>[http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/region "Region."] (Definition). [[Merriam-Webster]]. Accessed June 2011.</ref> Regional cuisines may vary based upon [[food]] availability and trade, varying [[climate]]s, [[cooking]] traditions and practices, and [[culture|cultural]] differences.<ref name="cuisine">[http://www.eldrbarry.net/hatr/eldrcuis.htm "The American Food Revolutions: Cuisines in America."] [http://www.eldrbarry.net Eldrbarry.net]. Accessed June 2011.</ref> One noteworthy definition is based upon ''traditional cuisine'': "A traditional cuisine is a coherent tradition of food preparation that rises from the daily lives and kitchens of a people over an extended period in a specific region of a country, or a specific country, and which, when localized, has notable distinctions from the cuisine of the country as a whole."<ref name="cuisine"/>
